terms.gloss: rent, hire (as the tenant or hirer)
evidence: Cic. Cael. 18: condūxit in Palātiō nōn magnō domum
Traupman 370; 215: autoraedam condūcere, to rent a car
terms.comment: The one who pays condūcit, the owner locat. A rented house is domus conductīcia (Lewis & Short s.v. conductīcius).

evidence: Plin. Ep. 9.37.3: sī nōn nummō sed partibus locem, if I let (the farms) not for money but for a share of the crop
terms.comment: Also to give out a job on contract; whoever takes it on condūcit (see contractor).

phrases.latin: in omnīque rē contrahendā, vendundō emendō, condūcendō locandō, vīcīnitātibus et cōnfīniīs, aequum, facilem, multa multīs dē suō jūre cēdentem
phrases.english: in every bargain, selling and buying, renting and letting, as a neighbour and over boundaries, (he should be) fair and easy, giving up much of his right to many

phrases.latin: cum domus patris ā forō longē abesset, quō facilius et nostrās domūs obīre et ipse ā suīs colī posset, condūxit in Palātiō nōn magnō domum
phrases.english: since his father’s house was a long way from the Forum, so that he could visit our houses more easily and be visited by his own friends, he rented a house on the Palatine, at no great price

phrases.latin: In quā domō habitat? — In quādam conductītiā. — Eho, nūllamne habet propriam domum? — Habet quidem, sed eam locat quibusdam inquilīnīs.
phrases.english: What house does he live in? — A rented one. — What, hasn’t he a house of his own? — He has, but he lets it to some tenants.

sources: Lewis & Short: conduco · Lewis & Short: loco · Lewis & Short: conducticius
